## Pull request overview

This PR fixes invalid JavaScript object syntax in MDX documentation blocks so that Next.js/Turbopack can successfully parse and evaluate embedded schema examples.

**Changes:**
- Replaced all `,,` occurrences in schema examples with valid single commas in `spacing`, `className`, and related properties.
- Corrected malformed object literals where `spacing: X, [` appeared by splitting into `spacing` and explicit `children` array properties.
- Verified there are no remaining `,,` or `spacing: N, [` patterns under `content/docs/blocks` after the changes.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated no comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `content/docs/blocks/authentication.mdx` | Fixes double commas and invalid `className` commas in authentication block schemas, restoring valid object syntax. |
| `content/docs/blocks/dashboard.mdx` | Cleans up extra commas and adds explicit `children` arrays where needed in dashboard examples to keep the schema objects parseable. |
| `content/docs/blocks/ecommerce.mdx` | Normalizes `spacing` and stack definitions by removing `,,` and ensuring valid property lists in ecommerce schemas. |
| `content/docs/blocks/forms.mdx` | Corrects multiple nested `stack` and layout objects by removing double commas and fixing `className`/`spacing` property syntax in form examples. |
| `content/docs/blocks/marketing.mdx` | Fixes invalid `spacing` and `children` definitions in marketing layouts, ensuring all example schemas are valid JS objects. |
</details>
